SMTO-EXE-0071 — The clipboard doesn't contain what SMTO asked for

GUID: 1f85e9ec-b757-5abb-8353-c69cc5fb919c
Slug: clipboard-format-absent
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO looked for text, files or an image on the Gateway computer's clipboard, but that kind of content wasn't there. The clipboard may be empty or hold something else.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, copy the text, file or image you want SMTO to use. SMTO reads the clipboard of the Gateway computer, not the device you're chatting from.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to read the clipboard again, saying whether it holds text, files or an image. SMTO only reads the clipboard when asked, and looks for one kind of content at a time.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the text, files or image you copied.

If it still fails

  • The app you copied from may use a format SMTO can't read; copy plain text instead, or save the image as a file. If that doesn't help, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway, without any private clipboard contents.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Clipboard format discovery or native retrieval found no value in the requested representation (text, files or image) on the selected Gateway's clipboard.

What this means

  • Clipboard format discovery or native retrieval found no value in the requested supported representation. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Clipboard format discovery or native retrieval found no value in the requested supported representation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect format metadata on the same Gateway; read content only under an explicit request.

How to fix it

  • Use clipboard.inspect to see which formats are present, then place content of the required type on the selected Gateway's clipboard (not the machine running the Server or browser UI) and issue a new explicit read. On Linux this also covers xclip or wl-paste reporting no selection or an unavailable target type.
  • Copy the desired content on the selected Gateway, then explicitly read it again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Copy the desired content on the selected Gateway, then explicitly read it again.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended content is deliberately copied and the requested format becomes available for an explicit read.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
